messages:
jess: main turned red immediately after PR merge (PR #6789). smoke/gpu-smoke-matrix failing with repeated OOMs on allocation step. job: smoke/gpu-smoke-matrix #42. logs: https://ci.redwood/inv/42 — seen in shard-3. anyone oncall or owner? feeling like an infra-induced regression :grimacing:
ci-bot: [automated] Pipeline 2233445566 failed on stage 'smoke/gpu-smoke-matrix' — failed tests: gpu_smoke::allocation_timeout x3. Console: https://ci.redwood/2233445566/console
oncall-bot: Paging eng-infra oncall: @matt — severity: build-red post-merge
matt: on it. pinging owners. can someone paste the failing snippet?
maria: grabbing logs now. looks like CUDA malloc failing with 'out of memory' when trying to reserve 12GB on node gpu-7. attaching short tail:
```
RuntimeError: [cuda] failed to allocate 12884901888 bytes: out of memory
  at runtime/alloc.cc:312
  at runtime/kernel_launch.cc:87
```

kai: hmm I saw a similar pattern yesterday when the kernel scheduler bumped mem prefetch. was that recent change in PR 6789? which commit hash?
jess: commit: a1b2c3d4 (merged by autosubmit). CI link shows the merge commit.
matt: okay, @kai I'll hand this to you to triage since it's GPU allocation related unless you object. If it looks infra, we can bisect. @maria can you trigger a rerun on that job (no cache) to confirm flakiness?
maria: running now: `/ci rerun 2233445566 --job smoke/gpu-smoke-matrix --no-cache`
ci-bot: Rerun queued: job smoke/gpu-smoke-matrix (rerun id: 2233445566-1). Estimated start ~30s.
(30s pass)
ci-bot: Rerun started on node gpu-9 (image: redwood/gpu-smoke:2026-03-16).
(90s pass)
ci-bot: Rerun result: FAILED — same OOM allocation in shard-3.
matt: consistent failure. let's bisect the merge range. @jess can you block on a temporary revert if bisect shows PR 6789 is culprit?
jess: yes, if bisect points to that commit we should revert to restore main.
kai: starting a quick git bisect across the last 5 merges. will narrow to candidate commits and run the smoke locally on a repro instance. I'll report back with reproducer or a suspect commit.
maria: for speed, also checking infra metrics — I see a big kernel driver upgrade rolled to gpu nodes two hours ago (drift: driver 525.85 -> 525.95). rolling back drivers is an infra path if needed. cc: @olivia infra PM.
olivia: saw the rollout. I can pause the driver rollout for the next 30m and roll back nodes that show OOM patterns. Hold off revert until we have bisect evidence?
matt: agree. priority: 1) bisect to identify culprit 2) if it's infra (driver) -> rollback 3) if it's PR change -> revert. kai, assigning to you as primary. please post bisect link.
kai: bisect run started: https://ci.redwood/bisect/2233445566-23 — running binary-smoke on each step. ETA ~12m.
(12m pass)
kai: quick update — bisect narrowed to commit a1b2c3d4 (PR #6789) altering allocator prefetch logic. reproducer attached: /artifacts/repro-2233445566.tar.gz. The change increases jemalloc arena reservation under certain sequence lengths.
matt: solid. @jess please open a revert PR for a1b2c3d4 and push hotfix to main to unblock. Maria/Olivia, coordinate rollback if revert doesn't resolve quickly.
jess: opening revert now: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/6790 (revert a1b2c3d4). requesting fast review from autosubsystem.
maria: rolling back driver rollout on nodes showing failure pattern as precaution. will monitor after revert lands.
ci-bot: New PR merged: revert PR #6790 merged to main. Triggering post-merge smoke run (build 2233445567).
ci-bot: Post-revert smoke run 2233445567: PASSED — all smoke/gpu-matrix shards OK.
matt: excellent — main green after revert. thanks team. kai, we should follow up with a safe rework of allocator change and perf regressions test in a sandbox before reintroducing.
kai: will draft a safer patch and add targeted GPU mem regression tests.
jess: filed follow-up issue to add targeted e2e to PR checklist. https://issues.redwood/INFRA-2142
matt: closing incident. summary: PR 6789 caused increased jemalloc reservation -> OOM on certain GPU nodes; revert restored green. follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
